e: if there is any doubt regarding payment of a pro forma invoice you should discuss it with a AtW Service Centre Team Leader. Examples may include payments outside UK/not directly to the supplier.

Pro forma invoices for ‘coping strategy’ sessions

Note: pro forma invoices for ‘coping strategy sessions’ are generally agreed at 12 sessions per customer. AtW will pay in advance on a pro forma invoice for 2 to 3 sessions at a time before committing to any further payments. This allows for any changes the customer may choose to make, for example, change of supplier, not all sessions being required, change of job etc.

if the customer has already completed the total number of sessions, AtW can reimburse for the full amount

the pro forma invoice will only be paid directly to the supplier.

Frequency of claims for on-going support

5. Encourage customers to:

make new claims on a regular basis, ideally on a 4 week cycle although variations are acceptable

only send in new claims after the last day for which payment has been claimed for

send us their claims within 6 months of the date the original spending was incurred

Note: Don’t issue pre-paid envelopes for the return of claim forms.

Forms in alternative formats

6. Information on types of alternative formats and reasonable adjustments can be found on the customer communications and accessibility intranet site.

Retention of documents

7. Claim forms and associated receipts or invoices in relation to Access to Work payments must be retained for 6 years after the financial year in which the transaction occurred.

8. Claim forms and associated receipts or invoices can be retained for a longer period as an exception if there has been an overpayment or a fraud interest.

9. Once the exception has ended; claim forms, receipts and invoices must be retained for a further period of 14 months.

Incorrectly completed claim forms

10. Payment teams mustn’t accept claim forms, where amounts have been amended or overwritten.

11. These should be returned to the customer with an explanation why it’s not possible to process the claim.

12. Ask the customer to send the claim back to us with mistakes corrected and signed against, not initialed, by the customer.

13. Claim forms signed prior to the last day for which support is claimed must be returned for re-signing at the appropriate time.

To claim travel to work costs

14. Travel to Work (TtW) is paid to support the customer with their journey to work.

15. Customers need to complete form DP226JP ‘Claim for travel to work costs’.

16. Parts 3 and 4 must be signed and dated by the customer and their employer

Note: If the customer is self-employed, Part 3 ‘Employer’s declaration’ doesn’t need a signature.

17. The form must show the total cost of the journey and the customer’s contribution towards it.

18. The full name, address and contact details of any taxi company used, must be supplied on an attached invoice/receipt.

19. Journey details should include pick up and drop off points.

20. If the invoice includes VAT, a registration number must be provided.

To claim travel in work costs

21. Customers wanting to claim travel costs during working hours, must complete form DP227JP.

22. Customers need to fully complete Part 2 of the form including:

pick up and drop off point details

total mileage

total cost

their contributions

their employer’s contributions

23. Invoices / receipts from a taxi company must include their full name, address and contact details. If the invoice includes VAT a registration number must be provided

Note: If the customer is self-employed, there’s no need to complete Part 3 ‘Employer’s declaration’.

To claim special aids and equipment costs

24. Before AtW can make a decision on a claim for one-off costs, AtW need a fully completed DP224JP form that is signed and dated by the purchaser. This could be the customer or the employer.

25. AtW also need original or certified copies of any invoices or receipts that support the claim.

To claim support worker costs

Payments to support workers

26. Case Managers can now obtain details from the SW Contract verbally, if the employer agrees. Case Managers will record details from the contract of employment in the Additional Info (Payment Team) field under the appropriate Element.

27. Customers or employers who do not wish to share this information by telephone can still continue to post or email (if a reasonable adjustment) any Contract of employment / Wage slip to Access to Work for Support Workers costs. Case managers will transfer the required contractual information into the Additional Info (Payment Team) field under the appropriate Element.

28. All claims for payments to support workers must be made on form DP222JP.

29. Claims for support worker costs, where the support worker works for either the customer directly or the customer’s employer must include:

a fully completed claim form signed by the customer and their line manager (not a third party)

full name of Support Worker

number of hours worked per week

total salary paid

total NI & Pension contributions made

any annual leave and/or sick leave taken during the period being claimed for

30. If the support worker works for an agency, they must supply:

days and hours worked

type of support provided

signed and dated by SW

details of the admin fee

Note: it is reasonable for Access to Work to request a payslip or timesheet when validating a claim for payment. This is to ensure the right level of funding is provided and subsequently reimbursed. Personal information should be redacted from the Timesheet / Wage slip. Only the information required to validate the claim will be used.

31. British Sign Language (BSL) support workers must supply a registration number and their level of qualification.

35. Where a customer has an existing claim but reports a change of circumstances that requires a new element unrelated to their existing element award, the civil servant will need to go to their employer for the new element. Their existing claim will continue until the award ends. The length of the existing award cannot be extended.

Examples

A civil servant customer has a TtW existing award which runs beyond 1 April 2022 and the customer requests help with SAE after 1 April 2022. The SAE element is a new requirement and therefore it’s a new claim. The SAE requirement is unrelated to their original award. The customer must speak to their manager about their required adjustment. As there was no change to the existing TtW award, the claim continues until the award ends. The length of the TtW award cannot be extended.

A civil servant customer has an existing award for a support worker which runs beyond 1 April 2022 and contacts us after 1 April 2022 to tell us about an increase in the support from the support worker and they now also need TtW support. The TtW element is a new application for support and unrelated to their original award. The customer must speak to their manager about their required adjustment. The increase in support from a support worker is a change of circumstances. The customer can receive an increased award, but the length of award cannot be extended.

Actions for Case Managers

36. Step 1. Once support is approved, check if the employment type has been recorded

Note: If the customer has changed job roles or department, their employment type may have changed.

You must identify and record the employment type if:

the type of government department employment has not previously been recorded in the Job field in DiSC or

their job role or department has changed

identify and record the employment type as:

Civil Servant as ‘Government Departments’, or

Public Servant as ‘Other Public Sector’

Step 2. Enter award end date in relevant fields Business case, Payment field

Note: If the customer is a civil servant, once the award end date has been set, the award must not extended for any reason.

Step 3. Issue the award letter ATW01

If the customer is a civil servant, select the appropriate dropdown

Step 4.In all cases a note must be created with the title ‘OGD Customer’ including:

confirmation that letters and claim forms have been issued with the appropriate text dropped in to the award letter.

if the customer is a civil servant, the following text with the customer’s award end date:

‘Fixed award end date of xx/xx/xx – Civil Servant. Do not extend funding beyond this date’

Apprenticeships

1. People serving apprenticeships are eligible for AtW support as they receive a wage and have a contract of employment. National minimum wage rates don’t apply to people on apprenticeships.

2. If the apprentice stays with the same employer when qualified, cost sharing status will remain unchanged for the whole of the AtW period of 3 years from the beginning of the apprenticeship.

3. For more information on UK apprenticeships visit the following websites for more information:

Apprenticeships in England

Apprenticeships in Scotland

Apprenticeships in Wales

3 Applications

Overview of application process

1. When dealing with applications for Access to Work (AtW) you must:

complete IT systems

contact the customer for additional information if required

update IT systems with additional information

Searchlight/CIS must be checked, to understand if a Correspondence address is recorded for the customer, that differs from that provided by the customer in their application.

if so, the customer must be contacted to confirm what address they want to use for AtW purposes.

if customer has a correspondence address and wishes to use this for AtW purposes, this must be noted in the additional information box in the customer’s record in DISC.

if following conversations with the customer and a change of address in Searchlight is required a CIS500 must be complete

Retrospective new applications

2. AtW will only consider funding from the point where all:

eligibility conditions have been met

requested evidence and information has been supplied and considered

support levels have been agreed

Note: Costs incurred by the customer/employer between the date of application and the date of decision, should be considered by the CM, and can be paid provided the above 3 points have been satisfied, or where the CM accepts that the customer has experienced exceptional circumstances. For example, being in hospital for an extended period, or having been misdirected by the Department.

3. Any costs that have been paid for prior to a new application being made and agreed will not be met by AtW.

Deferred applications

4. If a customer wants to check their eligibility for AtW before they apply, inform them to contact us again when they have decided to go ahead with their application. We will then review their eligibility.

Evidence

5. There’s usually no need to obtain condition corroboration from a suitably qualified medical practitioner or other relevant independent professional expert to assess a customer’s eligibility unless:

there’s a disagreement with the customer

there’s difficulty in determining whether the effect of the customer’s disability will introduce extra costs above those of a non-disabled person doing the job

6. Where there is insufficient information in the application to make a decision on the customer’s need for funding, case managers must contact the customer to gather additional verbal evidence.

If it becomes apparent that the customer is unable to work unaided after an extension period has been granted, consider what alternative support might be able to be funded from Access to Work to include SW or specialist aids and equipment

96. Any cut or withdrawal of support must be agreed with the customer and job coach.

97. A customer can ask for further help at any time if their circumstances change.

Mentoring

98. Access to Work does not offer support for mentors in the workplace. A Job Coach role is different to a mentor role in the workplace, mentoring in the workplace tends to describe a relationship in which a more experienced colleague shares their greater knowledge to support the development of an inexperienced member of staff.

99. Mentor support is a reciprocal and collaborative relationship that most often occurs between a senior and junior employee for the purpose of the mentee’s growth, learning, and career development.

Personal reader

100. Support is available for those needing help with reading. This may be due to dyslexia, blindness or sight loss.

101. They need access to text that cannot be provided by scanners or other specialist aids or equipment.

102. It’s likely to be used in conjunction with specialist aids or equipment but the 2 forms of help must not overlap.

103. Support may be used as an interim measure when a customer is waiting delivery of equipment or other support.

Travel buddy

104. This is someone who accompanies the customer when travelling to and from work. For example, where a customer has:

epilepsy

a visual impairment

fear of travelling such as agoraphobia and who cannot manage travelling alone

105. You may wish to consider this type of support for a short and decreasing period to allow someone newly disabled to become confident using public transport, rather than offer long term TtW support.

106. AtW would consider funding the transport costs involved with the Travel Buddy using the public transport.

Other

107. SWs can also deliver:

strategy training to help individuals with specific learning difficulties or mental health issues cope better in work

disability awareness training for colleagues and supervisors.

See: Mental Health and Support Services (MHSS) referrals

7 Adaptation to premises or equipment

Introduction

1. AtW is available to pay the additional costs to modify an employer’s or self-employed person’s premises or equipment to allow a disabled customer to work and stay in work.

2. This is only where it’s not the duty of the employer to make reasonable adjustments under the Equality Act 2010.

See: What are reasonable adjustments? on the Equality and Human Rights Commission website

3. What is reasonable will depend on:

the customer’s disability, illness or health condition and the effects of that disability, illness or health condition

how practicable the changes are

whether the change will overcome the disadvantage for the customer

how much money and resources are available

the cost of making the changes

4. The kind of adjustments which could be made include removing, changing or providing a way of avoiding a physical feature where it is reasonable to do so.

5. AtW funding cannot be used where there is a duty on the employer to provide facilities for disabled members of the public on their premises. For example; disabled access to public areas in a building.

6.This applies even if there are disabled employees who also need the facilities.

7. Examples of different types of adaptations for which help may be available are:

ramps for wheelchairs

lifts

the widening of doors

disabled toilets and washrooms

upgrades of computers and other equipment

Employer’s legal responsibilities

8. Employers must make adequate provision for disabled people present on their premises. This applies to both employees and visitors and takes into account all forms of disability.

9. You must be satisfied that the employer has taken action to carry out their legal responsibilities before ATW funding is allowed.

10. Employers have a number of legal responsibilities under the:

Factories Act, 1961

Offices, Shops and Railway Premises Act, 1963

Building (Fourth Amendment) Regulations, 1985

Chronically Sick and Disabled Persons (Amendment) Act, 1976

Building Regulations, Part M, or in Scotland, Technical Standards, Part T

Health and Safety Acts and other Regulations

Equality Act 2010

England and Wales – Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005and Fire Safety (Scotland) regulations 2006

Other European Union Regulations

11. These regulations cover:

access to premises

sanitary facilities

parking and

other aspects of a disabled person’s needs on working premises and buildings to which the public has access

12. For advice on current regulations, employers can contact:

local authority planning departments
